mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market momentum, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% signals accelerating industrial production, reflecting economic expansion and higher corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average +2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in FEDFUNDS below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth signals a strong easing response to recession risk, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.5% in one month AND GDPC1 annualized < 0% in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically greater than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, supporting consumer demand and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average +1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both GDPC1 and RSAFS month-over-month signals accelerating real personal spending and savings, indicating robust demand and confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent FEDFUNDS rate held at zero for more than six months in a negative GDP environment signals prolonged monetary accommodation, which initially boosts equities but eventually erodes yield compression benefits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS = 0% for >6 months AND GDPC1 annualized < 0% for >2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically less than zero at 5% significance.
